title: The Osero Artifact ships with named but unfilled parameters deferred to future Artifact iterations
content:
Four parameters in the Osero Artifact are present as documents but empty of content. A.6.1.1.7.2.1.1.3.1.1.4: "The address of Osero's Genesis Account will be specified in a future iteration of the Osero Artifact." A.6.1.1.7.2.1.4.2.1.1.4 and .1.1.5 say the same of the OSERO token address and Token Admin. A.6.1.1.7.2.1.4.2.1.2, covering minting and initial distribution, states only that "these processes will be defined in a future iteration."

The pattern is a deliberate alternative to two worse options: omitting the parameter (so its absence is invisible) or blocking the Artifact until every value exists (so nothing ships). Instead the slot is created, named, and explicitly marked unresolved.

This makes the Artifact's incompleteness itself governed information. Anyone assessing Osero can enumerate exactly what is undecided, and the deferred items are the ones that matter most for token holders — who controls the token admin and how the billion-unit Genesis Supply is distributed are unspecified while the supply cap is already permanent.

The tension worth flagging: a hard, irreversible commitment on supply (A.6.1.1.7.2.1.4.2.1.1.6) sits directly beside undefined distribution and admin control. The scarce quantity is locked before the question of who receives it has been answered.
description: Genesis Account, token address, token admin and the minting/distribution process are all placeholders — gaps declared in-structure rather than omitted from the governed text.
